previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on home hemodialysis, a mechanical aortic valve on anticoagulation, chronic diastolic heart failure, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for dark, tarry stools and weakness. She was found to have acute blood loss anemia with a hemoglobin of 8.0 g/dL and received three units of packed red blood cells. Evaluation with esophagogastroduodenoscopy, colonoscopy, and capsule endoscopy did not identify an active bleeding source, though angioectasia and polyps were noted. Warfarin was held and a heparin drip initiated, later transitioned back to warfarin. Her INR remained subtherapeutic at 2.2 at discharge, but she elected to leave with close outpatient follow-up. Hypertension was managed with increased labetalol, and dialysis was continued inpatient. She was discharged home with services, instructions to monitor for recurrent bleeding, check INR at dialysis, and follow up with vascular surgery and gastroenterology.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo woman PMH mechanical aortic valve, on 
coumadin, ESRD on home HD 5 days per week, who presented with 
GIB (melena).  During her hospital course she  required 5 units 
of pRBC over her hospital course. Coumadin was stopped on 
admission. She underwent EGD,capsule endoscopy, and tagged red 
blood cell study which did not reveal definitive source of 
bleed. While no source identified, bleeding may have been 
related to supratherapeutic INR (4.3 on admission). Bleeding 
resolved and coumadin was restarted at admission dose of 7.5 mg. 
On day of discharge INR was 2.9 (from 1.6 day prior) so coumadin 
was changed to 3 mg after discussion with pharmacy. Of note, 
goal INR is 2.5 to 3.5 for AVR.

Her calcium was noted to be persistently low which was 
attributed to ESRD. She was started on Tums and calcitriol 
during this admission per Renal recommendations.

# GIB: Ms. ___ presented with melanic stools and a drop in 
H/H.  She underwent EGD intially and capsule study which did not 
reveal a source of bleed. She then underwent tagged red blood 
cell study that was unrevealing.  She required 5 units pRBC over 
hospital course. Blood counts remained stable > 72 hours prior 
to discharge. 
 
# Mechanical Aortic Valve and supertherapeutic INR:  Although 
Ms. ___ presented with active GIB and supertherapeutic 
INR, mechanical aortic valves have high risk of clot, therefore 
did not reverse INR. Goal INR 2.5- 3.5. She was placed on 
heparin drip and eventually restarted on coumadin.  Initially

in INR.

week. Her calcium was noted to be persistently low which was

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital for bloody stools.  We did 
many tests, including looking at your stomach with a camera 
(EGD) and your small bowel with a pill (capsule endoscopy), 
which did not show any evidence of bleed. We believe this may 
have been spontaneous due to your elevated INR on arrival. We 
held your coumadin while you were bleeding and restarted it 
after you stopped bleeding. After restarting your coumadin, your 
blood counts were stable without any evidence of additional 
bleeding for several days.

We have decreased your home coumadin amount. Please have your 
INR checked on ___, and call Dr. ___ help with 
management. 

Lastly, we started 2 new medications on this admission 
(calcitriol and calcium carbonate). Please ensure that you 
continue them at home. 

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.
